name: Table
layerWhy: It shows rows to read across and down; what a table is about is the page's job.
promise: Rows of the same kind, read across and down, sortable by any column.
expectation: Column headers that sort, numbers lined up, and an empty table that says why.
evidence: Each header sorts ascending, descending, then back; it shows which way and announces it; numbers and dates sort by value.
behaviour: On by default; [sortable]="false" for a table, data-sort="false" for a column.
data-sort-value and <time datetime> sort by value.
With (sorted) bound, the data is sorted by you, not the rows.
context: Data people compare. Not for layout.
relationships: A .pr-table wrapper scrolls it within itself.
accessibility: Headers are buttons inside <th> with aria-sort.
The scroll wrapper is a focusable, named region.
failures: Never sorts a table whose order is its meaning.
dont: A table for a form layout.
